title: Move 1: The bisht edge
body:
Plain body; one rich line on the front edge and neck.

Keep the body of the garment plain. Put your one rich detail where the bisht puts it: down the front opening and around the neck.

- Men: a plain dark overcoat with a thin hand-finished braid only on the front edge.

- Women: the same edge on a long, open coat worn like an abaya.

- A Saudi eye reads "bisht". Anyone else just sees a well-made coat.

title: Move 2: Hidden comfort
body:
Soft cotton inside wool, like the labda.

The labda padded wool with cotton so it would not scratch. Copy the idea, not the look.

- A wool overshirt with a soft cotton lining inside.

- Nobody sees it. The wearer feels it every time.

- Tell the story on the inside label or the hangtag, not on the outside.

title: Move 3: One cut, two weights
body:
Same pattern in linen for summer, wool or camel for winter.

The bisht came in soft yarn for summer and coarse hair for winter. Same shape, different cloth.

- Summer: linen or a linen-cotton blend, light color.

- Winter: wool or camel hair, in brown or navy, the old Saudi winter colors.

- One pattern, two seasons. That is also cheaper to produce.

title: Move 4: The mekasar line
body:
Tone-on-tone silk stitching along the front.

Take the mekasar edge, silk stitching along the cloth's edge, and drop the gold. Stitch it in the same color as the cloth.

- Men: two thin rows of tone-on-tone silk stitching down a jacket's front.

- Up close it catches light. From across a room it disappears.

- Women: the same line on a long open coat, worn draped like a bisht.

title: Move 5: The barqa overcoat
body:
Long winter coat in undyed goat wool or camel hair.

The bisht al-barqa was hand-knitted from goat wool against cold desert nights. Bring back the idea: a long winter coat in undyed fiber.

- Undyed cream or brown goat wool or camel hair. No dye, so the fiber's natural color is the story.

- Long and loose, open at the front like a bisht.

- Name it after the barqa only on the label, for those who know.

title: Move 6: The honest label
body:
Fiber, micron, origin, trim type, written inside.

Luxury buyers trust what they can check. Put the facts a bisht maker would brag about inside the garment.

- Fiber and %, micron, country of origin.

- Trim type: say "gold-plated silver zari" only if it is true.

- This is also your shield: if a supplier won't give you these numbers in writing, don't buy.

title: Move 7: One Sadu motif, small
body:
One woven-in triangle band in two quiet colors.

Sadu is everywhere in souvenirs, so a big Sadu print reads cheap. Take one motif and shrink it.

- Weave one triangle band into a waistband, collar stand or bag strap.

- Use dobby or jacquard so it is part of the cloth, not printed on top.

- Two quiet colors only, like black and sand. Those who know will see it.

title: Move 8: Al-Qatt structure
body:
Triangle row and finger-width bands, color dropped.

Al-Qatt is a bright women's art. Keep its bones: the triangle row and the finger-width bands.

- Men: knit the triangle row into a sweater's hem or a scarf border, in black and sand.

- Women: the same band in one deep color on a long coat's hem.

- Never copy one family's wall. Use the rules, not a specific painting.

title: Move 9: Plant-dye palette
body:
Madder red, indigo, turmeric, loomi green.

Build a capsule using only the old plant colors: madder red, indigo blue, turmeric yellow, loomi green.

- Pick one main color and one accent per season.

- Natural dye varies a little: say so on the label and turn it into the story.

- Ask suppliers for color-fastness test results, because plant dyes can fade.

title: Move 10: Furjat vents
body:
Small triangle vents on the yoke and under the arm.

Najdi walls used small triangle openings to let air through. Give a summer overshirt the same job.

- A neat row of small triangle vents across the back yoke, where heat builds up.

- A short row under the arm, where you sweat most.

- Keep them small and in a line, so they read as a pattern, like on the wall.

title: Move 11: The roshan lining
body:
Lattice lining seen only when the coat opens.

The roshan lets you see out without being seen. Turn that into a secret inside the coat.

- A lattice-pattern lining, woven in, that only shows when the coat opens.

- Use cupro so the secret also breathes.

- Women: the same lining in a long open coat, flashing as she walks.

title: Move 12: Built for the Gulf
body:
Half canvas, half-lined in cupro, sleeves lined.

Your quality standard, written down once so every factory gets the same brief.

- Coats and bisht-style pieces: at least half canvas, never fused.

- Half-lined in cupro (Bemberg) for summer; sleeves always lined.

- Hand buttonholes on the top line. Inside unlined pieces, neat bound seams.

title: Move 13: The silent bell
body:
One closed silver bead; one coral-red stitch.

A woman's bell said "I'm here" without being seen. Turn it into a men's detail that says the same thing, quietly.

- One small closed silver bead on a drawstring end or a zip pull.

- No clapper inside, so it's silent. Only the wearer knows what it was.

- Inside a cuff: one stitch in deep coral red, a nod to ra'af beads.

title: Move 14: The munaykhal layer
body:
Open-weave overshirt over a solid base.

The Najdi overdress was a sheer "mesh strainer" layer over a solid dress. Keep the layering idea, change the shape.

- Men: a dark open-weave summer overshirt over a white thobe or tee.

- Sharper shoulders, straight cut, no embroidery.

- Women: georgette in Najd's muted grey or navy, long and wide-sleeved.

title: Move 15: The muted palette
body:
Najdi grey, navy, sand; one small accent.

Najdi women started with grey and navy before brighter colors arrived. That's already a quiet-luxury palette.

- Base colors: Najdi grey, navy, sand.

- One accent only: coral red (ra'af) or zari gold, used small.

- Use it for both men and women, so the brand looks like one family.

title: Move 16: The haskal pocket
body:
Slim inside pocket under the left arm.

Najdi men kept money in a pouch under the left arm. Put a slim inside pocket in the same spot.

- A slim inside pocket under the left arm of a jacket or coat, for a phone or cards.

- Lined in plant-tanned leather, the light Calligonum red.

- Women: the same pocket inside a long open coat.

title: Move 17: The khabt tab
body:
Small plant-tanned leather tab on the cuff.

Divers protected their fingers with small leather covers. Turn it into a small leather tab on a cuff or glove.

- A small plant-tanned leather tab on a shirt or jacket cuff.

- One silver snap only.

- Tell the diver's story on the hangtag.

title: Move 18: The red-cloth secret
body:
Deep red where only the wearer sees it.

Pearl prices were agreed by touching fingers under a red cloth. Put that red where only the wearer sees it.

- A deep red lining in a plain black or sand coat.

- Or one red-lined pocket.

- Pack each piece with an oud-scented card, not scented cloth (see the collar-pocket idea).
